chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abi al-Abbas, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him, 'Is there anything for the brothers from the mother (maternal brothers) from the blood money (diyah)?' He said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Blood money or compensation paid for murder or injury

ai.seo_question: Do maternal brothers inherit blood money (diyah) in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that maternal brothers (*ikhwān al-umm*) are excluded from inheriting the blood money (*diyah*) of a murdered relative, a ruling that highlights the distinct application of inheritance principles to compensation for homicide compared to general estate distribution. This distinction underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that *diyah* follows specific kinship lines, often prioritizing paternal lineage or direct descendants, thereby differentiating it from the broader categories of heirs in standard inheritance (*fara'id*).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Al Husayn, from Abu Al Abbas, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Is there anything for the brothers from the mother from the wergild?’
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn al- Haseen from abu al-‘Abbas who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
if brothers from mother’s side can receive any inheritance from the wergild. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, they cannot do so.’”
